Triggers.value: Visible injuries or wounds on others

Threat.value: I repeatedly check that doors and windows are locked
I wake during the night to check whether I am safe

Memory.value: When I remember the event I feel intense shame
The memory feels like it belongs to someone else rather than to me
When the memory returns I feel so overwhelmed by emotion that I have to stop

Negative Appraisals.value: You can never know who will harm you
I can't trust that I will do the right thing
I have permanently changed for the worse

vignette: Anaís had always taken pride in her independence and self-reliance. As a young Latin American woman working in a male-dominated field like HVAC repair, she'd grown accustomed to being one of the few women on a job site. But everything changed during a harrowing experience of torture at the hands of a group of men who targeted her specifically because of her gender. The event itself was etched into Anaís's memory with excruciating clarity: the feeling of being trapped and helpless, unable to escape or protect herself as her attackers inflicted pain on her body. Even now, the mere thought of those moments filled her with a sense of shame so intense it felt like she might suffocate under its weight. When memories of that day surfaced – and they often did, unbidden – Anaís would become overwhelmed by emotion, forced to stop whatever she was doing as grief and fear washed over her in waves. It wasn't just the memory itself that tormented Anaís; its very existence felt like a constant threat, reminding her of all the ways in which she couldn't trust others or herself. She began to see potential dangers everywhere: every woman who walked into the room could be hiding an ulterior motive; every visible injury on someone else's body was a grim reminder of what had happened to her own. Anaís found herself avoiding social gatherings where women might be present, opting instead for solitary nights spent huddled at home with doors and windows triple-checked. She couldn't shake the conviction that harm lurked around every corner, waiting to pounce if she let her guard down even for an instant. Anaís became hypervigilant, starting awake multiple times a night to reassure herself that the apartment was secure – the locks checked, the windows locked in place – before drifting off into fitful sleep once more. During the day, sudden noises or movements sent her jolting upright like a puppet on a string. The shame and self-doubt seeped into every aspect of Anaís's life, tainting even the things she loved most. She began to question whether she truly had what it took to succeed in her job, wondering if each minor mistake or setback was evidence that she'd never be more than a shadow of her former self. Her clients noticed the difference – the hesitation before responding to questions, the brittle laugh when discussing routine repairs. It wasn't until Anaís found herself frozen on a service call, unable to touch the injured hand of an elderly woman who needed help with her air conditioning unit, that she realized how far things had gone awry. She couldn't bear the thought of being trapped in this never-ending cycle of fear and self-doubt – it felt like torture all over again, but this time by her own hand. Anaís finally sought out professional help, acknowledging for the first time that she needed a safe space to confront these demons head-on. The prospect of therapy filled her with both hope and dread: what if, in the process of facing down these terrors, Anaís discovered that the damage truly was permanent – that some wounds would never fully heal?
